J1.evidence: TR translates the written text faithfully: أَتَّبِعُكَ بِإِذْلَالِي = 'kendimi alçaltarak sana uyayım', وَالْكَافُ صَاحِبُ الْحَالِ, (رَشَدًا) mafʿūl of تُعَلِّمَنِ, no ʿāʾid if object of عُلِّمْتَ, الرُّشْد/الرَّشَد two dialects. The variant بَاذِلًا لِي is put inside a marked [Mütercim notu: …], so it is not a silent change; it is also the reading of the printed Tibyān and is the one consistent with الْكَافُ صَاحِبُ الْحَالِ.

J2.evidence: TR renders the source as written: أَيْ أَتَّبِعُكَ بِإِذْلَالِي -> 'kendimi alçaltarak sana uyayım', وَالْكَافُ صَاحِبُ الْحَالِ -> 'kâf hâlin sâhibidir'. The variant بَاذِلًا لِي is only mentioned inside a marked [Mütercim notu: ...], which is allowed. It is also plausible, since the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl is the kāf (the addressee), which suits باذلا لي better than بإذلالي. رَشَدًا as the mafʿūl of تُعَلِّمَنِ and the ʿāʾid argument are correct.
